Updated Review:
So it is time to update this review. First about me: My wife and I have 4 kids with the youngest in diapers (we also use cloth diapers). So that being said, our washer and dryer are well used (at least one load a day if not more). We have a Kenmore Elite HE3t that we bought new from Sears in 2002. The only thing that has really gone wrong has been this pump. The original one lasted until November 2018. So that is when I bought my first replacement pump, this one right here that I am reviewing. When I bought it, it had a LIFETIME guarantee. Yes, a Lifetime guarantee on it. What can be better than a relatively inexpensive part (more than they are now) and a lifetime guarantee? I thought sold. Even if it breaks in a few years I can get a new one for free.

Well, it didn't make it a few years. It didn't even make a it a year. It broke in October of 2019, less than 11 months from when I installed it. But remember, it had a lifetime guarantee. So I contacted the manufacturer and they asked for some pictures and then had me order another one from Amazon. They then credited me through Amazon for the replacement. I thought that was pretty nice and that maybe I got a bad part since it broke in less than 11 months. So where did it break? It broke on the impeller. It cracked on the hub and came apart from the back piece. The motor also had water in it as I am assuming that is due to the seal failing when the impeller and hub came apart.

The product arrived on time, was heavier than the original pump motor which was nice. It fit in well and was an easy install. I liked that it came with a spare o-ring in case I ever need to remove it for any reason. Had no problems pumping water through an extended drain hose.
Was able to remove the old pump and put the new one in quick and easy.
